issues.legal_issue: The non obstante language added to the arbitration referral provision does not displace statutory exclusions from arbitration or override special and additional remedies provided by other laws.
material_facts: The buyer’s agreement contained an arbitration clause.
The consumer pursued a complaint before the consumer redressal forum and sought relief for alleged deficiency in service.
The application seeking referral to arbitration was made after the amendment to the referral provision.
issues.conclusion: The amendment limits judicial scrutiny of an arbitration agreement but does not override laws providing special or additional remedies, or make disputes non-arbitrable under those laws arbitrable.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(3) and 8(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, read with the amendment to Section 8, preserve other laws under which certain disputes may not be submitted to arbitration. The non obstante words in amended Section 8 were intended to limit judicial intervention concerning the arbitration agreement, not to displace special or additional remedies. The Court relied on Booz Allen and Hamilton Inc. v. SBI Home Finance Ltd., A. Ayyasamy v. A. Paramasivam, Vimal Kishor Shah v. Jayesh Dinesh Shah, and Ameet Lalchand Shah v. Rishabh Enterprises.

predicates.post_amendment_referral_application: A party sought referral to arbitration under the amended referral regime.
predicates.special_statutory_proceeding: A dispute was brought in a proceeding established by law for a particular statutory purpose.
predicates.special_statutory_remedy_applies: The law governing the dispute provides a special or additional remedy that may be pursued instead of arbitration.

issues.definition: When a referral request is made under the amended regime in a proceeding governed by a special statutory remedy, the amendment does not displace that remedy.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer forum is not required to refer a consumer complaint to arbitration when the consumer has chosen the statutory consumer remedy, despite an arbitration clause in the parties’ agreement.
material_facts: The consumer filed a complaint before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission seeking possession, financial adjustments, compensation, and other relief for alleged deficiency in service.
The buyer’s agreement contained an arbitration clause.
The company applied under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seeking referral of the dispute to arbitration.
The Commission rejected the application, and the Supreme Court found no error warranting review of its earlier dismissal of the company’s appeals.
issues.conclusion: The consumer forum was not obliged to refer the complaint to arbitration; the Commission’s rejection of the application was correct, and the review petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, makes the consumer remedy additional to other remedies. Sections 2(3) and 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, do not require referral where a consumer has elected the special consumer remedy. The Court relied on Fair Air Engineering Pvt. Ltd. v. N.K. Modi, Skypak Couriers Ltd. v. Tata Chemicals, National Seeds Corporation Ltd. v. M. Madhusudhan Reddy, Rosedale Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Aghore Bhattacharya, and Booz Allen and Hamilton Inc. v. SBI Home Finance Ltd.

rule.if: consumer_complaint_proceeding and consumer_chose_statutory_forum and contractual_arbitration_clause_invoked and arbitration_referral_sought

predicates.consumer_complaint_proceeding: A consumer brought a complaint before a statutory consumer redressal forum concerning goods or services.
predicates.consumer_chose_statutory_forum: The consumer elected to pursue the statutory consumer complaint as a remedy.
predicates.contractual_arbitration_clause_invoked: The opposing party relied on an arbitration clause in the parties’ agreement.
predicates.arbitration_referral_sought: The opposing party asked the consumer forum to refer the dispute to arbitration.

issues.definition: When a consumer pursues a statutory consumer complaint and the opposing party seeks referral based on an arbitration clause, the consumer forum is not required to refer the dispute.
